LESSON: CERAMIC MATERIALS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Materials for Production
Topic 3.2: Ceramic Materials
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Ceramic Materials, part of Materials for Production in Grade 8 PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How are ceramic materials used in day-to-day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify common ceramic materials in the locality,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Ceramic Materials in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. describe the physical properties of ceramic materials in the locality,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Ceramic Materials in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. relate ceramic materials to their use in a work environment,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Ceramic Materials in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. acknowledge the importance of ceramic materials used in the locality.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Ceramic Materials in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify common ceramic materials in the locality,

   Ceramic Materials helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. describe the physical properties of ceramic materials in the locality,

   Ceramic Materials helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. relate ceramic materials to their use in a work environment,

   Ceramic Materials helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. acknowledge the importance of ceramic materials used in the locality.

   Ceramic Materials helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss the meaning of ceramic materials,

2. use visual aids and realia to identify items made of ceramic materials (pottery, ceramic utensils, glass, shells),

3. collect items made of ceramic materials in the locality,

4. investigate the physical properties of ceramic materials (brittleness, fire resistance, heat resistance, water resistance, corrosion resistance),

5. visit the locality to explore the uses of ceramic materials,

6. use a chart to match ceramic materials to their uses in the work environment.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss the meaning of ceramic materials,
2. use visual aids and realia to identify items made of ceramic materials (pottery, ceramic utensils, glass, shells),
3. collect items made of ceramic materials in the locality,
4. investigate the physical properties of ceramic materials (brittleness, fire resistance, heat resistance, water resistance, corrosion resistance),
5. visit the locality to explore the uses of ceramic materials,
6. use a chart to match ceramic materials to their uses in the work environment.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Ceramic Materials together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: learner acquires evaluation and decision-making skills when collecting items made

of ceramic materials in the locality.

● Citizenship: learner demonstrates socio-cultural sensitivity and awareness when visiting the locality to explore the uses of

ceramic materials.

Values:
● Responsibility: learner engages in assigned roles and duties when collecting items made of ceramic materials in the locality.

● Unity: learner collaborates with others when using a chart to match ceramic materials with their use in the work environment.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety: learner observes safety precautions when investigating the physical properties of ceramic materials.

Link to other subjects:

Creative Arts: learner enhances skills of pottery when identifying items made of ceramic materials.

4. acknowledge the importance of ceramic materials used in the locality.

Remember the key question: How are ceramic materials used in day-to-day life?
